buffering.body:
A stream pauses when your connection delivers data slower than the video needs.

- Close other tabs, downloads and devices that use the same network.
- Move closer to the router or use a cable.
- Pause for a minute so the player can load ahead, then press play.
- Turn off a VPN, or choose a closer server in the VPN.
- Try again later. Sources are slower at busy hours.

The source decides which quality level is offered, so the picture sharpness may change during playback.

@@ diagnostics

buffering.summary: Improve a stream that keeps pausing to load.
buffering.title: Buffering, freezing or slow start

change-email-password.body: Open the profile menu and choose Account. Your details are under Account Details. Before a change we may ask you to confirm it's you, with your password or a code we email you. ## Password 1. Choose Password. 2. Enter your current password, then the new one twice. It needs at least 8 characters. 3. Choose Save. Changing your password signs out every other device at once, this one excepted, so anyone who knew the old password is out. ## Email 1. Choose Email and enter the new address. 2. Open the link we send to the new address to finish the change. ## Mobile phone and name Choose Mobile phone to add a number that helps you get back into your account, or Name to change your name. The main profile follows your first name.

cookies-explained.body: Cookies are small notes a website asks your browser to keep. Local storage is a similar place that only the site itself can read and that is not sent with every request. {brand} sets no cookies at all. No page and no request of this server sets one, and a test fails the build if any route starts to. In a browser, what keeps you signed in is held in this site's local storage; in an app, in the device's own secure store. That is the only thing kept on your device. Trailers can come from an outside video service, which can set its own cookies, and pictures come from a public film catalog. We do not control those. See Where titles come from. ## Your choices - There is no cookie banner and no cookie preferences page, because there are no cookies to choose between. - Personalised recommendations are off until you turn them on, and the answer belongs to the device you answer on. A second device starts off again. - If your browser clears site data, you are signed out on that browser. Your account keeps everything. @@ cookies

A description of the work you own. 3. The address of the page on {brand} that links to it. 4. A statement that you are the rights holder or are allowed to act for them. Send it to {support_email} with the subject DMCA notice. The full process is on the DMCA page.

delete-account.body: Deleting your account removes it straight away, with every profile, list, rating, setting and all viewing activity. It cannot be undone. One thing outlives it, and we would rather say so: the playback reports kept for 30 days (the time a title took to start, any failure and which source answered) lose the link to your profile at once, and each report is deleted as it reaches 30 days. An unused sign in code also keeps the address it was sent to until it lapses. 1. Open the profile menu and choose Account. 2. Choose Delete account at the bottom of the page. 3. Confirm it's you, then choose Permanently delete. If you only want to remove one person, delete their profile instead. See How to create, edit, or delete profiles. !! Note: To keep a copy of your data, download it first. See Download a copy of your data.

3. If playback works afterwards, add {brand} to the extension's allow list.

!! Note: We never ask you to install a browser extension or a codec to watch. Close any page that does.

kids-profile.body: A Kids profile only shows titles suited to children, with its own home page and menus made for kids. 1. Open Manage Profiles and choose Add Profile. 2. Type a name and turn on Kids Profile. 3. Choose Save. To turn an existing profile into a Kids profile, edit it and turn on Kids Profile. The main profile cannot be a Kids profile. To leave the Kids pages, choose Exit Kids and pick another profile. To stop a child from switching, lock the other profiles with a PIN. See How to add, edit, or remove a profile PIN. For older children, you can set an age rating on any profile instead. See Parental controls: age ratings and blocked titles. !! Note: Titles come from independent sources, and not every title carries an age rating. A Kids profile reduces what a child can find. It does not replace watching together. !! Note: A Kids profile only plays sources a finder has checked. The finder shipped with this project checks none, so on a server with no finder of its own a Kids profile may find nothing to play. need-account.body: Yes. You need a free account to watch on {brand}, and you must be 18 or older to create one. Creating one takes a minute and never asks for payment details. 1. On the {brand} home page, enter your email address and choose Get Started. 2. Enter your first and last name and choose a password of at least 8 characters. 3. Sign in with the address and password you just chose. If the address is already in use we email the person who holds it instead, and nothing changes. Your account keeps your profiles, My List, ratings, viewing activity and settings, so they are the same on every device where you sign in. Your first name becomes the name of your main profile. !! privacy-data.body: We do not sell personal data and we do not show ads. Here is the short version. The Privacy Policy has the full text. ## Kept in your account Your name, email address, an optional phone number, your profiles, My List, ratings, viewing activity and settings, a list of recent sign ins, and one technical card per signed in device describing what it can play. recommendations.body: Rows are made from what titles are: their genres, moods, subjects, country and decade, for example Feel-good Romantic Comedies or Korean Crime Series. Within a row, the order follows your taste. ## What changes your rows - What you start and finish, what you rate, and what you add to My List. - Rows such as Because You Watched, Today's Top Picks for You and Your Next Watch come from your recent titles. On a genre page they stay inside that genre. - The profile you use. Each profile has its own taste, and a Kids profile only shows titles for children. - The day and the season. Rows for holidays and events appear in their season. ## Turn it off Personalised recommendations are off until you turn them on, and the answer belongs to the device you answer on, not to the profile: signing in on a second device starts with it off again. Turn it off and you see the same picks as everyone else, and the taste worked out for the profile you are using is deleted. While it is on, we also keep a record of which rows you were shown, clicked and skipped, for 180 days. The Privacy Policy says what is in it. We never use your name or email to choose titles. See What data does {brand} collect? @@ data

sections.body:
This server sets no cookies. Not one page or request does, and a test fails the build if any route starts to: there are no advertising cookies, no analytics cookies, and none of our own.

What keeps you signed in is kept by the app you use, not sent as a cookie:
bullets: In a browser: the tokens for your session, in this site's local storage, which only this site can read.
In an app on a phone, a television or a computer: the same tokens, in the device's own secure store. On a device whose store refuses to keep them, your session lasts only as long as the app is open.
Nothing else. The server keeps no copy of your profiles, your settings or your viewing progress on your device, and no cookie carries your profile's name.
sections.title: What we keep on your device

sections.body: A trailer can come from an outside video service, which may set its own cookies when it plays. Posters and descriptions come from a public film catalogue, and video comes from independent sources. Your device loads those directly, so each of them can set its own cookies and see your IP address, as any site you open can. We do not control them and we tell them nothing about your account.
sections.title: Other sites

sections.body:
Clearing this site's data in your browser signs you out on that browser, and your account keeps everything. Signing out does the same on purpose.

Personalisation is off until you turn it on, and the answer belongs to the device you give it on: a second device starts off again. There is no cookie banner on this server and no cookie preferences page, because there are no cookies to choose between.

sections.body:
{brand} runs on a server that someone operates. That operator is the controller of your personal information and you can reach them at {support_email}. This policy describes the software as it is written, which is the same on every deployment, and it says plainly which few things the operator's own setup decides.

{brand} is a link aggregator and search engine: it does not host the films and series it shows. Signing in, the database and the recommendations all run on this one server. There is no separate accounts company and no outside recommendation service.
sections.title: Who we are

sections.body: We keep what the service needs, and this is all of it:
bullets: Your account: your first and last name, your email address, a mobile number if you add one, and your password, which is kept only as a scrambled (hashed) value.

Your profiles: up to five, each with a name, a picture, an age limit, its settings (autoplay, languages, subtitle appearance), a PIN if you set one, kept only as a hashed value, and the gender and player name you enter if you choose to.
What you watch: My List, your ratings, the titles you hide, how far you are through each episode, the reminders you set, and, while personalisation is on, the taste profile worked out from them.

Which rows you were shown: a record for each row impression, click, start, completion, like, skip and change to My List, per profile. We keep these only while personalisation is on for that session, and for 180 days.

Playback reports: each attempt to play something, with the time, how long the first frame took, any failure and which streaming source answered. These are kept only while personalisation is on for that session, and they do not say which title it was. The problem reports your app sends are separate: they carry its build and whatever you write in them, no profile and no account, and they are kept whatever you answer.

Your devices and sessions: the device name, hashed forms of the tokens that keep you signed in, a device key that names the device across sessions, and one technical card for each session: the app and its version, the kind of device, its system and version, its screen size, the codecs, containers and request headers its player handles, how much storage it offers, how it is controlled, and the languages it lists. The card is what decides which version of a title this device is offered.
Account events: one dated line for each sign in and each change to your account, kept 365 days. No screen shows this list to you yet; write to us for it.
Parental controls: a profile's age limit and the titles a guardian blocked by name, up to 200.
Sign in codes: the address a code was sent to and a hashed form of the code, until it is used.
Not your IP address. The server reads it to count requests and keeps it in memory for about a minute. No table stores it, and no history of your addresses or your locations exists anywhere.
sections.title: What we keep

sections.body:
Almost everything comes from you: what you type when you sign up, the profiles and settings you make, and what you do in the app. Your app adds two things of its own: the technical card that says what it can play, and the playback reports above.

We do not buy information about you and we are not given any by other companies. We do not look up where you are; the age ratings you see follow the region your own app asks for.
sections.title: Where it comes from

sections.body: Each use needs a lawful basis under the UK GDPR, shown in brackets. We use what we keep to:
bullets: run your account, profiles, My List, ratings and Continue Watching on every device you sign in on (contract);

keep the account safe: confirm it is you before anything sensitive, show you your devices, lock a profile after too many wrong PINs, and end every other session when you change your password (legitimate interests);
send the letters your account needs: a code to sign in, a link to set a new password, and a note if someone tries to open an account with your address (contract);
choose which rows you see and in what order, from what you watch, on a device where you have turned personalisation on (consent);
find and fix what breaks, from the playback and problem reports above (legitimate interests);
answer the messages you send us (legitimate interests).
sections.title: What we use it for

sections.body: Each of these is held by the code, not by goodwill:
bullets: No selling, no sharing for advertising. We do not sell, rent or trade personal information, and we give none of it to advertisers or data brokers.
No cookies at all. No page or request of this server sets one, and a test fails the build if any route starts to. There are no advertising or analytics cookies because there are no cookies.
No tracking across the web. There is no analytics service and no advertising tag in this product, and nothing we keep follows you to another site.
No IP addresses, no location history. As in the list above.
No age data. We do not ask how old you are and we do not check it, because we would rather not hold it.

Nothing built on your device's card. The technical card described above says what your device can play. It is not used to recognise you, it is not compared with other devices, and it does not leave this server. If you would rather we did not hold it at all, say so and we will tell you what the app needs.
sections.title: What we do not do

sections.body: Almost nothing leaves this server. Signing in, the database and the recommendations all run on the machine the operator runs, in a PostgreSQL that the server starts itself. There is one real processor, and then there are the places your own device talks to:
bullets: Mail. Your sign in codes, password links and account notes are handed to the mail service the operator configures. It is given the address the letter goes to and the text of the letter, and nothing else. On the deployment the maintainer of {brand} runs, that service is Resend (resend.com). Because this is software anyone can run, another operator can point it at a different service or at their own mail server; ask the operator of this server which one it is.

What your own device fetches. Posters, descriptions and trailers come from public catalogues, and the video comes from independent sources. Your device asks them directly, so they see your IP address and your request as any website you open does. We send them nothing about your account.
The law. We hand over personal information when the law requires it.
sections.title: Who else sees it

sections.body:
Your information lives in the database on the machine this server runs on, and the operator chose where that machine is. Nothing in the software puts data in a particular country, so this policy promises no region; ask the operator of this server where it runs and under which law they hold it.

The only personal information that leaves that machine is what the mail service above is given, and where that is processed depends on the service the operator chose.
sections.title: Where it lives

sections.body: Nothing is kept in case it is useful later. This is every store we have, with how long each lives:
bullets: Your account and its details: while the account exists. Deleting your account removes them at once.

Your profiles and what is in them: the profile, its picture, its PIN, its age limit and blocked titles, My List, your ratings, the titles you hide, viewing progress, settings, reminders and the notifications you dismissed, all while the profile exists. Deleting the profile, or the account, removes them at once.
The taste worked out from what you watch: while the profile exists. Turning personalisation off deletes it for the profile you are using.
Which rows you were shown: 180 days from each record, and only while personalisation is on for that session.

Playback reports: 30 days from each report, and only while personalisation is on for that session. Deleting your account removes your profile from them at once; the reports themselves go as each one reaches 30 days.
Problem reports your app sends: 30 days. These carry no profile and no account, so there is nothing in them to delete with your account.
Account events: 365 days.

Signed in sessions: until you sign out, or 30 days without use, whichever comes first. Changing your password ends every other session at once. On a television, signing other devices out asks for your password or a code first.
Your device list and the key in it that names a device: while the account exists.

Codes: a sign in code, and the code a television shows while it waits to be paired, until it is used or lapses. A sign in code you never use keeps the address it was sent to, and that stays true after the account is deleted.
Trailers that would not play, and the note of which changes your app already sent: the 300 most recent refusals per profile, and the notes while the profile exists.
Not about you: which certificate system each country uses, and counts of how often playback reached each source. No person is named in either, and deleting an account does not touch them.
On your device: what keeps you signed in, and nothing else. See the Cookie Policy.
sections.title: How long we keep it

sections.body: What protects your information here:
bullets: Isolation is enforced by the server, not asked for politely. Every statement that touches your data binds your account, and the key that opens a profile cannot be made anywhere but the door that has already checked your session. Code that forgot to check cannot read anything, which is a stronger guarantee than a database rule, and this database has no row level security rules.
Passwords and PINs are kept only in scrambled (hashed) form, and never put in a letter or a log.
Sensitive actions ask again. Deleting your account, asking for your data, changing your password and changing parental controls each need a fresh confirmation that lasts minutes.
A profile locks after too many wrong PINs.

Encrypted connections are the operator's to set up. This server speaks plain HTTP and expects the operator to put it behind HTTPS. If the address you are reading this on starts with https:// then they did.
No system is perfectly secure. If you think your account has been misused, change your password, which ends every other session at once, and write to us.
sections.title: How we keep it safe

sections.body:
Everyone who can sign in to your account can open its profiles and see their My List, ratings and viewing activity, unless a profile is locked with a PIN. The account holder can create, rename, lock and delete every profile.

The account holder can also move a profile to another account, named by its email address. The profile's whole library, its settings, its taste profile and its blocked titles go with it, and the person whose profile it is is not asked first. Choose carefully who you share your sign in with, and lock the profiles you want to keep private.
sections.title: Your account and profiles

sections.body: Under the UK GDPR you have these rights:
bullets: Access: ask for a copy of your data at any time, after confirming it is you. The file you get today holds your account details, your profiles and your devices. It does not yet hold My List, ratings, viewing progress, settings, your taste, reminders or the records listed above: write to {support_email} and we will send those too.

Erasure: delete your account at any time. Everything goes at once, except the playback reports named in the retention list: your profile is removed from them at once and each report goes as it reaches 30 days.
Rectification: change your name, email address and phone number yourself, or ask us to correct anything else.
Objection: turn personalisation off, or write to us to object to a use that rests on legitimate interests.
Restriction and portability: ask us to stop using your information while a question is settled, or to give it to you in a common machine readable format (JSON).

Withdrawing consent: personalisation is off until you turn it on, and your answer belongs to the device you give it on, not to the profile, so a second device starts off again. Turning it off deletes the taste profile of the profile you are using. It does not undo what happened while it was on.
Complaints: write to us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk.
sections.title: Your rights

sections.body: You must be 18 or older to open an account. We do not ask your age and we do not check it, because we would rather not hold it. Children watch through a Kids profile, or a profile with an age limit, that the account holder sets up and supervises; a Kids profile is only offered sources a finder has checked. We keep nothing about a child beyond what the account holder enters and what that profile does in the app. If you think a child has opened an account, write to {support_email} and we will delete it.
